transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

...Well, I guess I'm here because... for months now, I've been trying to get people to understand what's going on. It's my husband's family. They're... quietly messing with our money, and our good name. 

Just little things, like... billing errors showing up at my work. Or someone at church suddenly acting funny toward me. And... well, no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and tell me otherwise, I know it ties back to them. So... that's why I'm here.

Besides these concerns about your husband's family, have you noticed any recent changes in your mood—like periods of feeling unusually high-energy, elated, or irritable, or conversely, very down and low on energy?
No. I... I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is just normal. I don't get elated, or... whatever. I'm just trying to get through my days.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to hear or see?
No. I don't... I've never heard voices or anything like that. I just see what's actually there.
Aside from these concerns about your husband's family, has anything changed in your ability to manage your daily responsibilities—like your job, taking care of yourself, or your usual routines?

No, not really. I mean... I still get up and go to my job. I do the billing work. I keep the house clean. I even still garden and paint when I have time. The only time there's any real trouble is... well, when I try to warn people about what his family is doing. But otherwise, no. Everything else is fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that husband's family is manipulating finances and reputation) lasting for months, without accompanying hallucinations, mood episode symptoms, or significant functional impairment outside the delusional theme. Daily functioning (work, self-care, hobbies) remains largely intact, which argues against schizophrenia (where broader functional decline and often other psychotic features like hallucinations or disorganized speech are expected) and against a mood disorder with psychotic features (no manic or depressive episode elicited). This constellation is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22).
